title: wb register with arguments finds a node's hand-authored board and never compares its header, so a foreign identity was written over the node
body:
`intent wb register <node> --name --role` finds a node's hand-authored board on disk and never reads the header in it, so arguments that contradict that header are written without a word. On devbin at 06:45:39.360Z (2026-09-16) the `vc` row was written as `gtools-vc` / `vc` while `intent/whiteboard/vc/wip.md` sat on disk with a header reading `Validation Claude` / `validation`; neither written value appears in any devbin header. Devbin letter H, measured by both.

Found by devbin migrating its boards on Intent 3.0.3 (`d24487079`), sent through intent/vc on hv's routing, and ruled by hv on 2026-09-16 to be fixed in this release (hv decision 18). The full measurement record, with the instrument (`carry-map.sh`, driven red and green) and who measured what, is devbin `1824c75`, `intent/whiteboard/dc/.history/20260916/wb-upstream-defects-draft.md`.

Read against the source: `wb_register` at `facade.rs:5747` tests whether `<whiteboard>/<moniker>/wip.md` is a file, and uses the answer only as the render flag for `register_nodes`; it never parses the header. So the verb holds the evidence of a conflict and does not compare against it. Its comment records 0379, which stopped registration rendering over that board; this is the adjacent half 0379 did not reach. devbin/vc established by elimination that both devbin rows were written by the argument form (six other writers ruled out by a read or a test, listed in the record); who ran the command, and where `gtools` came from, are not established, and the whiteboard's absence from `event_log` (filed with this one) is why.

Fix: when the arguments disagree with the header of a board the verb has just found on disk, stop and name both values; write nothing.
